text:
marta: Heads-up — p90 token latency for pool dedicated-eu-2 jumped ~35% after last night's runtime roll. Saw it during synthetic load test and a couple customer traces.

infra-bot: ALERT: dedicated-eu-2 p90_token_latency > 80ms (now 113ms) — triggered at 1782456805.

raj: Which rollout did we run? kernel-selector bump? batching heuristic tweak?

marta: We deployed kernel-selector=v2.3 + batching:dynamic_flush=on. No other infra changes.

sophia: Initial profiling shows larger KV fetch variance. Quick query: promql -> avg_over_time(kv_cache_miss_rate{pool="dedicated-eu-2"}[1h]) jumped 2% -> 12%.

lee: I pulled a token-level trace sample. Breakdown (median -> p95): kernel_exec 5ms -> 13ms, kv_fetch 3ms -> 23ms, queue_wait 2ms -> 4ms. So kv_fetch tail is main regressor.

raj: Interesting. Did kernel-selector change fallback behavior that might evict or bypass KV cache? Could be different memory layout/quantization causing cache-insensitive access pattern.

marta: That was my hypothesis. We observed more full KV cache misses when sequences hit exact lengths that trigger kernel path alpha.

lee: Here's the raw trace snippet (sampled):
```
TRACE_ID=tr_9af3
tokens: [..]
kernel: selected=gpu_q4_compat_v2.3
kv_cache_hit=false
kv_fetch_time_ms=21.2
kernel_exec_ms=12.7
```

sophia: We should add labels to the token latency metric for kernel_selector and kv_cache_hit. Right now token_latency_seconds is only by pool+route. Need per-token breakdown in dashboards.

raj: Agreed. Metric proposal (Prometheus):
```
# counter/gauge examples
redwood_runtime_kernel_select_total{pool,model,kernel_version} 1
redwood_runtime_kv_cache_hit_total{pool,model,route,hit="true"} 42
redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket{pool,route,kernel_version,kv_hit}  ...
```
This lets us split p50/p90 by kernel and kv behavior.

marta: For dashboards: add a stacked p95 panel showing kernel_exec vs kv_fetch vs queue_wait (per-route). Also add per-pool kernel_version distribution and kv_cache_miss_rate heatmap.

devops-bot: NOTE: created ticket PF-4521 "instrument token_latency by kernel and kv_hit" assigned to eng-runtime.

lee: Short term mitigation: canary rollback kernel-selector to v2.2 on dedicated-eu-2 and see if miss rate drops. Alternatively create a new pool (dedicated-eu-2a) and route hot routes there.

marta: I'll run a canary rollback tonight and run the synthetic tests. If rollback doesn't help we spin up dedicated-eu-2a.

raj: Also tweak batching heuristic: prefer flush_after=shorter when kv_cache_miss_rate rises above X to avoid high tail from long KV fetches piling up. Might reduce throughput but improves latency SLO.

sophia: We should add an alert: kv_cache_miss_rate > 5% sustained for 10m -> page oncall. Also a regression alert: kernel_version change + p90_token_latency delta > 20% -> create an incident.

marta: Action items:
- marta: run canary rollback tonight, post results.
- raj: add metric labels for kernel_version + kv_hit (PF-4521) (start with counters/histograms).
- lee: dashboard panels + heatmap mockups, add alert rules.
- sophia: validate sampling tracer includes kernel and kv flags.

marta: Will post a follow-up run log. Thanks all :thanks: 

devops-bot: reminder: scheduled autoscale window for dedicated-eu-2 at 2026-03-18T02:00Z. If we need isolation, request before that window expires.

marta: noted — requesting pool split if rollback doesn't cut it.

lee: If we isolate, let's reserve 1 node for the noisy model to avoid cross-pool interference.

raj: One last perf tip — add a sampled counter for kernel_path_changes_per_request to see how often selector flips mid-request. Could point to instability causing cache thrash.

marta: Great. I'll update PF-4521 with these extra metrics and link the dashboard PR.

sophia: Thanks, will prep the alert runbook if pager trips.

marta: End of thread for now — will update after rollback test (1782457060).
